summary: Direct Floquet analysis of the forced jet orbit at Re = 2000: one real multiplier, -1.1577, outside the unit circle (period doubling); the other converged multipliers lie inside.
description: Krylov-Schur (k_dim = 128, mode 3.11) on the map that takes a perturbation of the forced orbit to its value after one forcing period, T = 1 / 0.6. The orbit is the one of 210_baseflow_newton. Spectre_Hd.dat holds the Ritz values with their residuals; Spectre_Hd_conv.dat holds the converged multipliers by decreasing modulus, and Spectre_NSd_conv.dat the same as growth rate sigma = ln|mu| / T and frequency. The run stops at step 57 of 128, when the leading multiplier has converged (residual 1.4e-10) and has stood still for 5 steps; 13 Ritz values then meet the tolerance 1e-6. The other converged values lie on an arc inside the unit circle (modulus 0.93 to 0.84) that moves with the step at which the run stops, so they are not checked. The orbit closes to 4.6e-5 in the relative velocity norm (printed as Orbit closure in logfile). The leading multiplier is real and negative: the orbit is unstable by period doubling, with sigma = 0.0878. The mode norms are those of the mode files written by the solver, whose normalisation does not change between runs. The values are those of the run named under produced.

leading_multiplier.note: Real part of the leading Floquet multiplier; it is negative, so the instability doubles the period.

leading_sigma.note: Growth rate ln|mu| / T of the leading multiplier.

leading_mode_vx_norm.note: Norm of the axial velocity of the leading mode; its sign is arbitrary, the norm is not.

leading_mode_vy_norm.note: Norm of the radial velocity of the leading mode.
